form.label: Correlation 2 Sources
form.description: Find the same entity (service, user, or host) active across TWO data sources within a time window.

search.query: | rest /services/data/indexes | search (title=london_* OR title=berlin_* OR title=loc1_*) | table title | sort title
| rest /services/data/indexes | search (title=london_* OR title=berlin_* OR title=loc1_*) | table title | sort title

ul.li: A data source is a system sending its logs to Splunk. Each one lands in its own index — think of an index as a labelled bucket of events (here: $srcA$ and $srcB$).

Correlation means connecting events from different systems that share something in common — the same user, service, or host — around the same time. One system only shows its own slice; correlation reveals the whole story (e.g. the same user active on two servers).

ol.li: Search both indexes at once: (index=$srcA$ OR index=$srcB$)
Pick a shared field to line them up on — the Correlate by control above (service / user / host). That's $key$ right now.
Group with stats and count how many events came from each source per key.
Keep only the keys that appear in both sources — those are the correlated ones.

ul.li: How to read this page: the chart shows whether the two sources are active at the same times; the table lists every $key$ seen in both $srcA$ and $srcB$, with a count from each. The exact search is shown at the bottom.

html.p: Tip: change Correlate by to user to show the same person active across both systems — the classic "one identity, many systems" story.

search.query: (index=$srcA$ OR index=$srcB$) | rex field=_raw "\s(?<service>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_\-./]*)(?:\[\d+\])?:\s" | rex field=_raw "(?i)(?:user[=:\s]+|for\s+)(?<user>[A-Za-z0-9_.\-$]+)" | eval src=if(index=="$srcA$","A","B") | stats count(eval(src=="A")) as A, count(eval(src=="B")) as B by $key$ | where A>0 AND B>0 | stats count as correlated

panel.title: Events over time — do the sources light up together?

search.query: (index=$srcA$ OR index=$srcB$) | timechart span=5m count by index

panel.title: Correlation table — $key$ present in both $srcA$ and $srcB$

search.query: (index=$srcA$ OR index=$srcB$) | rex field=_raw "\s(?<service>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_\-./]*)(?:\[\d+\])?:\s" | rex field=_raw "(?i)(?:user[=:\s]+|for\s+)(?<user>[A-Za-z0-9_.\-$]+)" | eval src=if(index=="$srcA$","A","B") | stats count(eval(src=="A")) as A_events, count(eval(src=="B")) as B_events, min(_time) as first, max(_time) as last by $key$ | where A_events>0 AND B_events>0 | eval "First seen"=strftime(first,"%F %T"), "Last seen"=strftime(last,"%F %T") | rename A_events as "$srcA$", B_events as "$srcB$" | table $key$ "$srcA$" "$srcB$" "First seen" "Last seen" | sort - "$srcA$"

html.pre: (index=$srcA$ OR index=$srcB$) | eval src=if(index=="$srcA$","A","B") | stats count(eval(src=="A")) as A_events, count(eval(src=="B")) as B_events by $key$ | where A_events>0 AND B_events>0
html.p: Swap the Correlate by field or the two sources above to tell a different story (same user on two hosts, same service across sites, etc.).
